newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil orange growers say firms blocking exports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil orange growers say firms blocking exports.

text.p: Brazilian orange growers have complained that a small number of firms have a stranglehold on export facilities and are blocking small growers' access to transport, storage and ships, the anti-trust body Cade said.

"We have received some complaints from orange growers saying that the industry has adopted some anti-competitive practices, principally in the export sector," said council member Renault de Freitas Castro, who is handling the case.
The complaints were directed at four firms which dominate the Brazilian frozen orange juice export market -- Cutrale, Citrossuco, Cargill and Citrovita, said Castro.

The Association of Citrus Growers of Sao Paulo State (Aciesp) and the Brazilian Association of Citrus Growers (Associtrus) said small growers were facing problems getting access to transport, loading and ships.

They also complained of restricted access to chilled storage facilities in the port of Santos and filed a complaint against chilled storage company Frigorifico Avante in Minas Gerais state, according to Castro.
Cade has asked the Ministry of Finance to inspect the four large firms and produce a report on which it will base its ruling.
The intention is to check the records on use of terminals, transport and warehousing. It's a first stage of investigation into the type of use of these facilties," said Castro.
If Cade finds that the complaints are justified, it can order firms to change their practices or even impose fines.
Castro said he was also reviewing the reporting practices of ten citrus firms who last year signed an agreement to stop negotiating in block.
"I concluded that the reports have some faults which need to be corrected," he said. "Some of them are very patchy."
In the reports, the firms are expected to give an account of their dealings with growers and any changes in commercial practices.
